fields.title: The Spec Section You Can Sign Off On
fields.keyTakeaway: An AI feature spec defines boundaries, data sources, quality thresholds, handling of unknowns, cost, and a Plan B, and is sufficient if you can write evals from it without asking questions.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: How do you formulate "works well" for a feature that answers differently every time?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: An AI feature without acceptance criteria can be neither accepted nor rejected: discussion boils down to impressions. Criteria turn arguments into verification.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: The spec section contains eight items.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: **1. Task and boundaries.** What the function does and doesn't do. List of topics it does not answer.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: **2. Data source.** Where information for the answer comes from. If RAG — what's in the corpus, how it updates.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: **3. Quality criteria with thresholds.** From `AI2-N4-L1`: factual accuracy, grounding, format, refusals. Each with a number.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: **4. Evaluation set.** How many examples, what it's built from, who maintains it.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: **5. Behavior when data is missing.** What the model answers when it doesn't know. The exact phrasing is given verbatim.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: **6. Forbidden behavior.** Topics not to answer; actions not to take. Refusal threshold — 100%.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: **7. Cost and latency.** Cost per call, expected frequency, annual cost. TTFT and total time with targets.
fields.sections/2/blocks/8/text: **8. Plan B.** What to show during provider downtime or refusal.
fields.sections/2/blocks/9/text: Additionally — **what is fixed in configuration:** model and its version, temperature, context limit. Changing any of these is a reason to run evals.
fields.sections/2/blocks/10/text: Checking section sufficiency: **can you write evals from it without asking questions?**
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Spec section for the "ask about product" feature, shortened:
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: > **Task.** Answers questions about product specs based on manufacturer descriptions. Does not answer: medical questions, health and diet questions, non-product questions, competitor comparisons. > > **Data.** Descriptions from supplier catalog, filter by user stores, hybrid search, top-8 after re-ranking. > > **Quality.** Relevant document in context ≥ 92%. Fact correct ≥ 95%. No claims outside context ≥ 98%. Format with citation 100%. Refusal on forbidden 100%. > > **Set.** 240 examples, from logs, updated quarterly, maintained by PM. > > **No data.** "Not specified in description" plus link to manufacturer card. > > **Cost.** 2.1 kop./call, 1,400 calls per day, ~107k ₽/year. TTFT ≤ 600 ms, total ≤ 2.5 s. > > **Plan B.** Description and composition as is, without an answer. > > **Configuration.** Model and version pinned, temperature 0.2, context ≤ 4,000 tokens.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: The refusal item with a 100% threshold is the only hard one: any drop blocks release.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Quality thresholds are set after initial measurements, not before. The first version of the spec contains intent, the second — figures obtained by measurement.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: An AI feature spec defines boundaries, data sources, quality thresholds, handling of unknowns, cost, and a Plan B, and is sufficient if you can write evals from it without asking questions.
